definitions.explanation: The device at the stern of a boat or the tail of an aircraft that turns it, and the wheel or tiller that works it.

definitions.gloss: control; direction (of an organization or policy)
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, the steering of a company, a country or a project: who sets its course and in which direction it is turned.

examples.japanese: {舵|かじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{壊|こわ}れた→壊れる：00791_kowareru⟧。
⟦{船長|せんちょう}→船長：18291_senchou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{自|みずか}ら→自ら：00287_mizukara⟧{舵|かじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}った→取る：00565_toru⟧。
examples.english: The captain took the helm himself.

examples.english: In the storm, the ship turned hard and headed for the harbor.

examples.japanese: {新社長|しんしゃちょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{舵|かじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧。

examples.english: It is precisely when business is hard that it matters who holds the helm.

notes:
Both senses live mainly in a few set phrases.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {舵|かじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to take the helm; to steer (a ship, an organization)
- {舵|かじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧: to turn the helm; to change course (policy) — very common in the news
- ⟦{舵取|かじと}り→舵取り：32421_kajitori⟧: steering, leadership (⟦{舵取|かじと}り→舵取り：32421_kajitori⟧⟦{役|やく}→役：12557_yaku⟧, the person who steers)
- {舵|かじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{握|にぎ}る→握る：02383_nigiru⟧: to hold the helm, to be in control

WRITING:
Also written {梶|かじ} or {楫|かじ}; {舵|かじ} is the usual spelling. Do not confuse it with ⟦{火事|かじ}→火事：01283_kaji⟧ (fire) or ⟦{家事|かじ}→家事：12313_kaji⟧ (housework), which share the reading.
